name: OLD MAID
description: Old Maid is a timeless children's card game focused on matching and evasion. Using a standard deck with one card removed (or a specialized deck), players aim to pair up all their cards and discard them. The tension lies in the final unmatchable card—the 'Old Maid'. The player left with this card at the end of the game loses. It is a game of simple mechanics, bluffing, and luck.

content.text: Old Maid is a timeless children's card game focused on matching and evasion. Using a standard deck with one card removed (or a specialized deck), players aim to pair up all their cards and discard them. The tension lies in the final unmatchable card—the 'Old Maid'. The player left with this card at the end of the game loses. It is a game of simple mechanics, bluffing, and luck.
Dates back to the early 19th century. It likely evolved from older gambling games where the loser had to pay for drinks ('Black Peter' in Germany, 'Le Pouilleux' in France).
Standard cards. Remove the Queen of Clubs. The Queen of Spades becomes the 'Old Maid'.
Standard 52-card pack with one Queen removed, or a dedicated Old Maid deck.
Deal all cards out one by one. It doesn't matter if some players have one more card than others.

items.text: Black Peter: A Jack is removed instead of a Queen; the holder of the odd Jack at the end loses. Often played with a special 31- or 37-card pack where the odd card depicts a black cat or chimney sweep.
Reversed Old Maid: Same mechanics but the holder of the odd card (last Queen or Old Maid) at the end is the winner instead of the loser.
Dedicated Old Maid Pack: Special pack of matching pairs plus one Old Maid card (e.g. comical character); the single Old Maid card has no pair and its holder loses.
